Exact choice: Reference 300 s and query 300 s; half-open windows
Source / lineage: TD-v1.3 registered design; no external optimum claimed
Scientific purpose: Give equal-duration baseline and incident support while keeping the estimator local to the known injection
Why this exact value/range: 300 s is a pre-outcome compromise between sample support and temporal locality
Alternatives considered: 180/300/420 s query-horizon sensitivity; 300 s registered primary
Development observation: C1 L/O changed across horizons but the headline O<=L pattern remained
Known limitation: Not a universal optimum; fixed windows may blur short transients
Allowed claim: The window is a registered operational choice with bounded sensitivity
Prohibited claim: 300 s is theoretically optimal for all incidents
Defense answer: We used equal 300-second baseline and incident windows for enough bins without abandoning temporal locality; we tested 180 and 420 seconds and do not claim universality.

Exact choice: 10 s bin width
Source / lineage: TD-v1.3 registered design; data cadence and sparse-count trade-off
Scientific purpose: Align metric and trace evidence on a common grid without making count channels excessively sparse
Why this exact value/range: 10 s is the primary compromise; no paper establishes it as optimal
Development observation: Performance varied materially; bin20 approached parity while bin5 degraded both arms
Known limitation: Temporal aggregation changes both signal and sparsity
Allowed claim: 10 s is the registered primary and temporal aggregation is a material limitation
Prohibited claim: 10 s is optimal or development proves 20 s should replace it
Defense answer: Ten seconds is a registered compromise between resolution and support; the strong bin sensitivity is disclosed, not used to retune the method.

Exact choice: Metric bin requires >=5 distinct observed seconds
Scientific purpose: Prevent a bin with only a few repeated or bursty samples from representing a 10 s interval
Why this exact value/range: Five seconds demands evidence over at least half the bin; exact cutoff has no external optimum
Development observation: Loader audit made support/missingness observable; no direct 3/5/7-second comparison
Known limitation: Exact cutoff rationale is not centralized in TD prose
Allowed claim: It is a conservative support guard, not a performance-tuned detector threshold
Prohibited claim: Five seconds is statistically optimal or literature-mandated
Defense answer: We require observations across at least half of a ten-second bin so a burst does not masquerade as interval coverage; the exact five-second cutoff is study-specific.

Exact choice: Valid channel requires >=24/30 finite bins in both reference and query
Scientific purpose: Keep normalization and ranking from being driven by heavily missing channels
Why this exact value/range: 24/30 is an 80% completeness convention aligned with the study's broader eligibility policy
Alternatives considered: Drop channel below gate; missingness remains explicit
Development observation: Development loader audit verified actual coverage
Known limitation: Exact 80% cutoff has no external optimum and no direct OFAT
Allowed claim: The gate conditions whether evidence is usable; it is not an efficacy threshold
Prohibited claim: The gate was selected because it maximized MRR
Defense answer: We require 80% finite support in both windows so scale and anomaly summaries are not based on sparse fragments; it was fixed before outcomes.

Exact choice: Center = median; scale = max(IQR, relative floor, 1e-12)
Source / lineage: BARO arXiv:2405.09330 supports median/IQR robustness; GDN arXiv:2106.06947 and official evaluation code use median/IQR error normalization; PRIOR SUPPORTS PRINCIPLE, NOT EXACT PARAMETERIZATION
Scientific purpose: Provide robust per-channel comparability under outliers and short windows
Why this exact value/range: Median/IQR resist outliers better than mean/SD; exact floor composition is a study adaptation
Alternatives considered: Mean/SD not registered; floor sensitivities registered
Selection policy: Fixed primitive; floor selected on development
Development observation: Phase 2 found the 1e-12 branch can dominate C5 loss; it did not establish a C1 outcome cause
Known limitation: IQR can be zero on sparse counts; transfer from prior work does not validate exact floors
Allowed claim: Robust normalization is principled and exact safeguards are study-specific
Prohibited claim: Prior work proves this complete formula is optimal
Defense answer: Median and IQR are robust choices for short noisy windows; our two-floor safeguard is an adaptation whose sparse-count limitation is explicit.

Exact choice: NumPy/type-7 empirical quantiles
Source / lineage: Conventional linear empirical quantile definition; TD fixes implementation semantics
Scientific purpose: Make Q90, quartiles and IQR reproducible
Why this exact value/range: Type 7 is a standard convention and is fixed to eliminate library ambiguity
Development observation: No evidence of implementation drift
Known limitation: Small samples can differ across quantile conventions
Allowed claim: The convention ensures exact reproducibility
Prohibited claim: Type 7 is uniquely correct
Defense answer: We fixed a standard quantile convention so every implementation returns the same values; it is a reproducibility choice, not a scientific optimum.

Exact choice: Relative floor epsilon_rel in {0.001,0.01}; selected 0.01
Scientific purpose: Limit amplification when IQR is small relative to channel magnitude
Why this exact value/range: Two orders of magnitude form a small predeclared robustness set; development selected 0.01
Selection policy: Development selected using registered C1 selection
Sensitivity evidence: Both variants evaluated; broader floor sensitivity also reported
Development observation: C1 selected 0.01; outcomes remained sensitive to temporal/scaling choices
Known limitation: Does nothing when median(abs(x))=0 and IQR=0
Allowed claim: It is a bounded numerical-robustness choice, not a universal floor
Prohibited claim: 0.01 is theoretically optimal
Defense answer: We compared two preregistered relative safeguards and selected 0.01 on development; the zero-median case is not solved by this term.

Exact choice: Absolute fallback 1e-12
Source / lineage: TD-v1.3 numerical safeguard; Phase 2 sealed-artifact diagnosis
Scientific purpose: Avoid division by zero when both IQR and relative scale vanish
Why this exact value/range: 1e-12 is a numerical nonzero fallback, not a meaningful physical scale
Selection policy: Fixed before development; diagnosis only after development
Sensitivity evidence: Relative-floor variants do not alter zero-median/zero-IQR cases
Development observation: Phase 2: real extreme effects and lambda-loss dominance, but lag3 recovery with identical affected scalers refuted a single-cause explanation
Known limitation: Can create enormous normalized values for sparse count channels; existing OFAT did not isolate a causal performance effect
Allowed claim: It prevents undefined arithmetic and must be disclosed as a non-decisive limitation
Prohibited claim: 1e-12 is scientifically calibrated or harmless
Defense answer: It was a preregistered divide-by-zero safeguard; development exposed an extreme sparse-count behavior, so we retain the sealed analysis, disclose the limitation, and do not retrofit the method without causal evidence.

Exact choice: Per-bin deviation r=abs(x-center)/scale
Source / lineage: Robust anomaly-score lineage from BARO/GDN; PRIOR SUPPORTS PRINCIPLE, NOT EXACT PARAMETERIZATION
Scientific purpose: Measure magnitude of departure irrespective of sign on a comparable robust scale
Why this exact value/range: Absolute magnitude matches the ranking estimand, which asks which service is most anomalous rather than direction of change
Alternatives considered: Signed deviation and other norms not registered
Development observation: Produced usable local ranking L=.744206 MRR on development30
Known limitation: Discards direction and depends on scale quality
Allowed claim: It is a transparent robust magnitude score
Prohibited claim: It identifies causal direction or is universally best
Defense answer: We rank how unusually large the departure is, not whether it rose or fell; that is appropriate for localization but not causal interpretation.

Exact choice: Temporal pool = Q90; max is sensitivity
Scientific purpose: Capture sustained/high anomaly while reducing single-bin domination
Why this exact value/range: Q90 is a high-tail summary below max; exact 0.90 is a registered convention
Development observation: Primary Q90 was selected; max sensitivity did not reverse the broad negative graph result
Known limitation: No external optimum; Q90 may miss very brief spikes
Allowed claim: Q90 balances persistence and peak robustness within the registered design
Prohibited claim: Q90 is universally optimal
Defense answer: We use a high quantile so one isolated extreme does not fully determine the channel; max remains a registered sensitivity.

Exact choice: Metric-channel pooling = max or Q90; selected Q90
Scientific purpose: Reduce multiple metric channels to one modality score per service
Why this exact value/range: Q90 limits single-channel domination while remaining tail-sensitive
Sensitivity evidence: Both candidates included in local selector
Development observation: Selected Q90 was stable enough for the registered run; no universal claim
Known limitation: Channels are heterogeneous and pooled without learned weights
Allowed claim: This is a transparent, bounded service-level reducer
Prohibited claim: Q90 is a learned optimal feature combiner
Defense answer: We compared max and Q90 within the preregistered registry and used Q90; it is deliberately simple and auditable.

Exact choice: Modality fusion = max or available-mean; selected available-mean
Scientific purpose: Combine metric and trace evidence without imputing absent modalities
Why this exact value/range: Available-mean gives equal contribution only among present modalities; max represents an OR rule
Sensitivity evidence: Both candidates evaluated; fixed-fusion sensitivity reported
Development observation: Available-mean selected; fixed-fusion sensitivity stayed near the primary C1 result
Known limitation: Equal weighting is not learned and availability can vary
Allowed claim: It is a missingness-aware, transparent fusion rule
Prohibited claim: It proves metrics and traces are equally informative
Defense answer: We average only available modality scores to avoid treating missing data as normal; equal weighting is a design convention, not an empirical truth.

Exact choice: Trace count transform = log1p(distinct trace/span count)
Source / lineage: TD-v1.3 trace feature definition; conventional count compression
Scientific purpose: Stabilize heavy-tailed counts while retaining zeros
Why this exact value/range: log1p is defined at zero and compresses multiplicative count differences
Alternatives considered: Raw count not registered as primary
Sensitivity evidence: Temporal bin sensitivities indirectly change count sparsity
Development observation: Trace-count sparsity contributed to zero-scale cases
Known limitation: Does not make counts Gaussian and can hide absolute-volume meaning
Allowed claim: It is a transparent variance-compressing transform
Prohibited claim: log1p is proven optimal for these traces
Defense answer: We use log-one-plus-count because counts are heavy-tailed and include zeros; it improves numerical behavior without claiming a distributional model.

Exact choice: No interpolation; unavailable channels/modalities remain missing; root absent => failure score 0
Scientific purpose: Prevent fabricated evidence and keep failures comparable across arms
Why this exact value/range: Conservative policy makes absence visible rather than silently inventing values
Development observation: Development completed with explicit quality limitations
Known limitation: Conservative zero for root-absent mixes data failure with ranking failure by design
Allowed claim: Claims include data availability and method performance under the registered pipeline
Prohibited claim: Missingness is proof of normality or zero means the method ranked the root last
Defense answer: We do not invent observations; if the root is not rankable the case receives zero, making data failures visible in efficacy.

Exact choice: Primary C1 uses metrics plus traces; logs excluded
Source / lineage: TD-v1.3 scope; common-input fairness for L/O/R
Scientific purpose: Keep the estimand focused on graph propagation over numeric service evidence shared by all arms
Why this exact value/range: Metrics and trace counts are alignable and complete enough for the common scorer; log semantics would add a separate representation problem
Development observation: Development result is therefore about M+T evidence only
Known limitation: Cannot generalize to all observability modalities
Allowed claim: Claims are limited to the registered metric-and-trace C1
Prohibited claim: The study proves logs add no value
Defense answer: We isolate the graph question using common numeric metric and trace evidence; adding logs would change both representation and estimator, so it is outside this estimand.

Exact choice: BARO-style robust local baseline
Source / lineage: BARO arXiv:2405.09330; PRIOR SUPPORTS ROBUST LOCAL PRINCIPLE, NOT TD DATA ADAPTER
Scientific purpose: Provide a strong non-graph robust anomaly-ranking comparator
Why this exact value/range: BARO contributes median/IQR-based local deviation suitable for limited noisy data; TD fixes its own channel and case adapter
Alternatives considered: Registered local L and LocalMAX comparators
Sensitivity evidence: Same development30 cases and evidence audit
Development observation: BARO development MRR was about .659120, below registered local L
Known limitation: Adapter and multimodal pooling are not the original BARO experiment
Allowed claim: BARO is a prior-work-informed local comparator
Prohibited claim: TD results reproduce all BARO claims or prove BARO inferior generally
Defense answer: We include BARO as a recognizable robust local baseline, while limiting claims to our adapter and benchmark.

Exact choice: LocalMAX secondary local aggregation
Scientific purpose: Check whether the selected local pooling benefits merely from a more conservative max rule
Why this exact value/range: Max is the simplest high-tail alternative with no graph and no learned weights
Development observation: LocalMAX MRR about .741178, close to L=.744206
Known limitation: Near-equality does not prove pooling irrelevance; sample is small
Allowed claim: It contextualizes the selected local aggregation
Prohibited claim: LocalMAX validates the selected registry or replaces the primary
Defense answer: LocalMAX is a simple no-graph stress comparator; its closeness to L shows the local result is not driven by a large pooling advantage.

Exact choice: RCD baseline through fixed RCAEval adapter; localized causal discovery with registered discretization/defaults
Source / lineage: RCD NeurIPS 2022 arXiv:2203.14883 and official RCAEval implementation; PRIOR SUPPORTS ALGORITHM, NOT TD ADAPTER
Scientific purpose: Compare graph-propagation ranking with a distinct causal-discovery RCA family
Why this exact value/range: Use the published/official implementation path with a frozen adapter rather than reimplementing or tuning it on outcomes
Alternatives considered: No adapter search; method-specific failure policy fixed
Sensitivity evidence: Adapter and failure audits; no rerun in this review
Development observation: Completed development result is interpreted only under the adapter's eligible inputs
Known limitation: Discretization, time-column removal, imputation and benchmark mismatch limit transfer
Allowed claim: It is a reproducible external-family comparator
Prohibited claim: Observed trace graph becomes a causal graph or RCD result proves causality
Defense answer: RCD is included as a fixed prior-work comparator; its causal assumptions and adapter limitations are not transferred to our observed dependency graph.

Exact choice: Observed dependency graph from resolved parent-child spans in the reference window
Source / lineage: Trace data semantics plus TD-v1.3 construction rule
Scientific purpose: Use case-specific executed dependencies rather than a static architecture guess
Why this exact value/range: The reference window avoids incident-label leakage and represents actually observed calls
Alternatives considered: Static graph and randomized controls; no causal graph claim
Development observation: Development graphs included isolates and variable degrees; these were analyzed post hoc
Known limitation: Missing/incomplete traces yield missing edges; observed edge is not causal
Allowed claim: The graph encodes observed execution dependency in the specified window
Prohibited claim: Observed trace edges are causal edges or complete architecture
Defense answer: We build the graph from parent-child spans actually observed before the incident; it is an execution-dependency graph, not a causal graph.

Exact choice: Raw directed edge caller u -> callee v
Scientific purpose: Preserve the direction of service invocation
Why this exact value/range: Caller-to-callee follows the trace relation rather than a learned orientation
Alternatives considered: Reverse and undirected operators act on this raw graph
Sensitivity evidence: Directed, reverse and undirected registered operators
Development observation: No source-semantics conflict found
Known limitation: Parent resolution errors can remove or misassign edges
Allowed claim: The raw direction means invocation, not root-cause direction
Prohibited claim: Caller-to-callee proves causal influence
Defense answer: The edge says who called whom in the trace; the diagnostic propagation direction is a separate modeling choice.

Exact choice: Reverse-call PPR operator
Source / lineage: MicroRCA IEEE DOI:10.1109/NOMS47738.2020.9110353 and official code reverse the anomaly graph before PageRank; NetworkX PageRank documents incoming-link propagation; PRIOR SUPPORTS PRINCIPLE, NOT EXACT TD GRAPH
Scientific purpose: Propagate local anomaly mass from affected callees toward plausible upstream callers
Why this exact value/range: Reverse direction matches the diagnostic intuition that downstream symptoms can point back toward an upstream origin
Sensitivity evidence: Reverse and undirected candidates plus damping grid
Development observation: Undirected d=.5 won registered development selection; reverse variants did not dominate
Known limitation: Invocation reversal is a heuristic, not a causal guarantee
Allowed claim: Reverse-PPR has prior lineage and a clear diagnostic interpretation
Prohibited claim: MicroRCA validates this exact dataset/operator or reverse edges are causal
Defense answer: Prior RCA work reverses call edges for PageRank-style localization; we adapt that intuition and test it rather than treating it as causal truth.

Exact choice: Undirected graph variant
Scientific purpose: Test whether adjacency carries useful association when direction is incomplete or ambiguous
Why this exact value/range: Undirected is the simplest direction-agnostic comparator using the same nodes and edges
Sensitivity evidence: Registered operator comparison and post-hoc mechanism analysis
Development observation: Undirected d=.5 was selected but O=.702405 remained below L=.744206; margin and leave-cell stability were limited
Known limitation: Can reward hubs and cannot express cause direction
Allowed claim: It is a robustness alternative for incomplete direction, not a causal model
Prohibited claim: Undirected selection proves direction is irrelevant
Defense answer: We included an undirected variant because trace direction may be incomplete for diagnosis; its selection is empirical and does not convert association into causality.

Exact choice: For positive local mass, p=(l/max(l))/sum(l/max(l)); sum(l)=0 gives a common all-tie/no-evidence result, never uniform PPR
Source / lineage: Personalized PageRank definition in NetworkX; MicroRCA-style anomaly personalization; PRIOR SUPPORTS PRINCIPLE, NOT EXACT SCORE OR ZERO-MASS POLICY
Scientific purpose: Anchor propagation in observed anomaly evidence instead of pure structural centrality
Why this exact value/range: The C1 estimand is the incremental effect of graph propagation over the same nonzero local evidence; zero evidence must not let topology invent a ranking
Alternatives considered: Uniform-positive personalization is a label-free diagnostic only, not the zero-mass fallback; degree centrality is not primary
Sensitivity evidence: L/O/R share the same local vector and zero-mass rule
Development observation: Development selected configuration had no all-tie/empty/zero local case
Known limitation: PPR inherits local score-scale biases; positive uniform personalization can induce topology ranking but is not the primary zero-mass behavior
Allowed claim: O differs from L by controlled propagation on common evidence; zero local mass remains a common all-tie
Prohibited claim: Zero local mass falls back to uniform PPR or lets topology rank services
Defense answer: When local evidence has positive mass, it becomes the personalization vector; when all local evidence is zero, every arm returns the same no-evidence tie rather than allowing topology to manufacture a ranking.

Exact choice: Damping d in {0.2,0.5,0.85}; selected 0.5 with undirected graph
Source / lineage: 0.85 is conventional PageRank/MicroRCA reference; 0.2 and 0.5 form a bounded study grid; PRIOR SUPPORTS PRINCIPLE, NOT EXACT PARAMETERIZATION
Scientific purpose: Span weak to strong reliance on graph travel while retaining personalization
Why this exact value/range: Three preregistered values cover low, balanced and conventional-high propagation without a search continuum
Sensitivity evidence: All six registered PPR candidates and leave-cell checks
Development observation: Undirected .5 selected by a small advantage; O still underperformed L and selection varied across held-out cells
Known limitation: No theorem or external evidence makes .5 optimal; small development sample
Allowed claim: 0.5 is the registered development choice for final confirmation
Prohibited claim: 0.5 is globally optimal or scientifically privileged
Defense answer: We included low, middle and conventional-high damping; development selected 0.5, but we present it as a registered choice, not an optimum.

Exact choice: Self-loop for isolated nodes
Source / lineage: Markov-chain/PageRank well-posedness convention; TD-v1.3 explicit rule
Scientific purpose: Keep an isolate's mass defined rather than dropping the service or creating a dangling-row ambiguity
Why this exact value/range: A self-loop is the minimal topology-preserving completion for an isolate
Alternatives considered: Uniform dangling redistribution would mix unrelated services
Development observation: Isolate-associated harms were post-hoc and not causal; 17/17 local-rank1 cases stayed rank1
Known limitation: Self-loop means graph contributes no new neighbor evidence for that node
Allowed claim: It is a numerical/topological completion with explicit semantics
Prohibited claim: Self-loop demonstrates self-causation or isolate harm authorizes gating
Defense answer: An isolate self-loop keeps the transition matrix defined and preserves its local mass; it carries no causal interpretation.

Exact choice: PPR primary graph operator
Source / lineage: PageRank/PPR canonical mechanism; MicroRCA reverse-PPR lineage
Scientific purpose: Provide a normalized mass-conserving propagation estimator directly comparable across cases
Why this exact value/range: PPR naturally accepts local personalization and exposes a single damping control
Alternatives considered: Degree/centrality; value diffusion; GNN outside estimand
Sensitivity evidence: Damping/direction grid; R topology control; value diffusion secondary
Development observation: Primary O did not improve over L on development30
Known limitation: Negative development result is valid evidence; PPR is not proven beneficial
Allowed claim: The primary tests a prespecified graph-propagation hypothesis
Prohibited claim: PPR is retained because it won or must beat local
Defense answer: PPR is primary because it cleanly tests whether graph propagation adds value over fixed local evidence, not because we assumed it would win.

Exact choice: Value diffusion secondary; alpha in {0.2,0.5,0.85}
Source / lineage: TD-v1.3 separates value smoothing from probability-mass PageRank
Scientific purpose: Check whether neighbor smoothing behaves differently from stationary mass redistribution
Why this exact value/range: Same bounded strengths aid interpretation while keeping the operator mathematically distinct
Development observation: Best diffusion development MRR about .720162, also below L
Known limitation: Not a substitute confirmatory result and values are not probabilities over nodes in the PageRank sense
Allowed claim: It is a secondary operator robustness check
Prohibited claim: Diffusion and PPR are interchangeable or secondary results rescue the primary
Defense answer: PPR redistributes probability mass; diffusion smooths scores. We keep diffusion secondary so those meanings and claims are not mixed.

Exact choice: L/O/R use identical local evidence and case support
Scientific purpose: Attribute O-L to the observed graph operator and O-R to topology rather than upstream score differences
Why this exact value/range: Common evidence is required for an interpretable paired comparison
Development observation: Development aggregate recomputation matched sealed results
Known limitation: Only isolates the graph operator effect within the registered evidence representation
Allowed claim: O-L is the incremental graph-operator effect for this registered pipeline
Prohibited claim: O-L is a universal value of graphs
Defense answer: All three arms start from the same local scores; the comparison changes the graph treatment, not the evidence.

Exact choice: R uses degree/component-preserving edge switches
Source / lineage: Graph randomization design in TD-v1.3; aligned with null-model principle
Scientific purpose: Destroy specific topology while preserving coarse confounds such as node set, degree and components
Why this exact value/range: This null asks whether observed wiring matters beyond those coarse properties
Alternatives considered: Unconstrained Erdos-Renyi rejected; directed/undirected switch kernels
Development observation: All 30 development cases completed and were mobile under descriptive gate; R=.678235
Known limitation: Preserving degree/components does not preserve every structural property; topology diagnostic has no predictions
Allowed claim: R is a structured negative control, not a generic random graph
Prohibited claim: R removes all graph structure or proves causality
Defense answer: We randomize wiring while preserving degree and component constraints so the control is difficult in the specific way relevant to O-versus-R.

Exact choice: 256 independent chains per eligible case/operator
Scientific purpose: Estimate randomized-graph outcome distribution without a single lucky graph
Why this exact value/range: Power-of-two ensemble balances Monte Carlo stability and fixed compute budget; exact number is operational
Sensitivity evidence: Topology feasibility inspected across all chains
Development observation: 30 cases x 6 topology jobs completed; 46,080 draws
Known limitation: No direct chain-count convergence sensitivity; independence depends on seeded chains
Allowed claim: 256 is a prespecified Monte Carlo budget adequate for descriptive null estimation
Prohibited claim: 256 guarantees convergence or effective independence
Defense answer: We fixed 256 seeded chains to avoid single-random-graph conclusions; it is a compute-and-stability budget, not a theorem.

Exact choice: Primary switch proposal budget = 200E
Scientific purpose: Allow many local edge-switch proposals scaled to graph size
Why this exact value/range: Scaling by E makes the budget comparable across case sizes; 200 is the registered middle value
Development observation: All budgets passed descriptive development mobility checks
Known limitation: Mobility checks do not prove Markov-chain mixing or independence
Allowed claim: 200E is a registered central budget supported by bounded mobility sensitivity
Prohibited claim: 200E proves stationarity/mixing
Defense answer: We scale proposals with edge count and use 200E as the registered middle budget; 100E and 400E check mobility, not formal mixing.

Exact choice: Mobility gate: >=32 unique final graphs; median edge overlap <=0.8; pass >=80% cases and >=50% each final root stratum
Scientific purpose: Prevent a frozen randomization kernel from supporting a topology claim
Why this exact value/range: Thresholds demand visible movement globally and within root strata; exact cutoffs are operational safeguards
Development observation: Development summary reports 30/30 cases mobile and the descriptive 80% gate true
Known limitation: No external optimum; development check is descriptive and the final root-stratum gate remains unopened
Allowed claim: The gate conditions whether R evidence is interpretable
Prohibited claim: Passing proves perfect mixing or unbiased random graphs
Defense answer: The mobility gate is a preregistered minimum-quality condition: enough distinct endpoints and limited overlap, including root strata; it is not a convergence theorem.

Exact choice: Forecast next-bin signal then score residual anomaly
Source / lineage: GDN arXiv:2106.06947 supports graph-based prediction/residual anomaly detection; PRIOR SUPPORTS PRINCIPLE, NOT EXACT LINEAR MODEL
Scientific purpose: Test whether dependency context improves short-horizon anomaly detection
Why this exact value/range: Prediction error provides a common target for G/L/ALL while keeping the model auditable
Development observation: G and ALL exceeded L on primary development, but capacity/context confounding remains
Known limitation: Prior work does not validate TD's ridge features, windows or pooling
Allowed claim: C5 evaluates contextual forecasting under the registered design
Prohibited claim: GDN validates this exact detector or G-L is purely graph structure
Defense answer: We use forecast residuals because context should help predict normal behavior; the exact linear model is our controlled, reproducible adaptation.

Exact choice: G, L and ALL feature arms
Scientific purpose: Separate own-history evidence, graph-neighbor context and their combination
Why this exact value/range: Three arms expose whether context adds predictive capacity and whether combination helps
Sensitivity evidence: Same targets/scalers; sealed feature masks and variants
Development observation: G/ALL strongly outperformed L in primary, while lag3 let L recover
Known limitation: Arms differ in feature capacity/context, so G-L is not a pure graph-structure causal effect
Allowed claim: The arms compare registered feature families
Prohibited claim: G>L proves graph structure alone caused the gain
Defense answer: G, L and ALL are controlled feature-family ablations, but G versus L still differs in available context and capacity, so attribution is limited.

Exact choice: Own lag plus same-type caller/callee means and coverage fractions
Scientific purpose: Represent local temporal persistence and aggregate neighborhood context without node-specific parameter explosion
Why this exact value/range: Means and coverage are permutation-invariant, bounded-complexity summaries compatible with missing nodes
Development observation: Context arms performed well on development; no pure structural attribution
Known limitation: Mean aggregation loses heterogeneity and degree can affect support
Allowed claim: Features operationalize additional dependency context transparently
Prohibited claim: These features are optimal or identify causal parents
Defense answer: We use simple neighbor means and coverage so the graph contribution is inspectable and reproducible; they summarize association, not causality.

Exact choice: 5 s bins and 180 s warmup prefix
Scientific purpose: Provide more forecast points than C1 while staying near the injection
Why this exact value/range: Five-second bins give 36 warmup points; 180 s bounds the pre-injection history
Alternatives considered: 10 s bin and 240 s prefix registered sensitivities
Development observation: bin10 materially improved L-MTL; prefix240 did not
Known limitation: Strong bin sensitivity and no external optimum
Allowed claim: Primary timing is registered and sensitivity is material to interpretation
Prohibited claim: 5 s/180 s are universally best
Defense answer: We fixed a short five-second forecast grid and three-minute history, then disclosed that binning materially changes L behavior rather than retuning after outcomes.

Exact choice: First 24 bins/120 s fit; final 12 bins/60 s held-out calibration
Scientific purpose: Select regularization on pre-injection fit history and threshold on a disjoint normal calibration tail
Why this exact value/range: Two-thirds/one-third gives enough rows for fitting while retaining a temporally later threshold block
Alternatives considered: Prefix240 sensitivity changes support; no alternate split grid
Development observation: Primary L-MTL remained low under prefix240; G/ALL remained high
Known limitation: Small per-case sample and temporal dependence
Allowed claim: Fit and threshold calibration are separated before the incident
Prohibited claim: Calibration is independent IID evidence or split is optimal
Defense answer: We reserve the last normal minute for threshold calibration so the incident and final labels never tune the detector; the split is a study design, not an IID guarantee.

Exact choice: V_fit frozen at fit boundary; scored targets require registered availability
Scientific purpose: Prevent later observations from changing which nodes the model knows
Why this exact value/range: Freezing membership at the fit boundary makes all target identities pre-incident
Development observation: Completed sealed runs preserved target identities
Known limitation: New services after fit cannot be scored and coverage may differ by arm
Allowed claim: Membership is leakage-safe within the registered window
Prohibited claim: The method handles arbitrary dynamic topology
Defense answer: We freeze the modeled node set before calibration and injection so later evidence cannot alter eligibility.

Exact choice: Lag1 primary; lag3 sensitivity
Scientific purpose: Test immediate next-bin predictability with minimal parameter count
Why this exact value/range: Lag1 is the lowest-capacity autoregressive baseline for short warmup; lag3 tests modest extra history
Development observation: Lag3 raised L-MTL from about .07 to about .65 while affected 1e-12 scaler identities stayed the same
Known limitation: Primary collapse is not explained by scale alone; lag1 may underfit dynamics
Allowed claim: Lag1 is a parsimonious registered estimand with material lag sensitivity
Prohibited claim: Lag1 is optimal or scale pathology alone caused L collapse
Defense answer: We chose lag1 to keep the primary model low-capacity; lag3 is a sensitivity and its recovery shows model history matters materially.

Exact choice: Ridge regression with numerical linear solve
Source / lineage: Standard L2-regularized linear regression and stable numerical solve
Scientific purpose: Control small-sample multicollinearity and keep coefficients reproducible
Why this exact value/range: L2 shrinkage is a low-variance choice for correlated features with only a few fit rows
Alternatives considered: OLS and nonlinear models not primary
Development observation: All sealed variants executed deterministically
Known limitation: Linear/additive assumptions can underfit and sample size is small
Allowed claim: Ridge is an auditable regularized forecaster
Prohibited claim: Ridge is the best forecasting model
Defense answer: We use ridge because it is stable and interpretable in a small-sample correlated-feature setting; it is a baseline, not a superiority claim.

Exact choice: Lambda grid {0.1,1,10}; selected 10 by equal-weight G/L/ALL pre-injection MAE
Scientific purpose: Choose regularization without incident outcome labels while preventing one arm from determining the shared lambda
Why this exact value/range: One decade below/at/above one spans weak to strong shrinkage without dense search
Selection policy: Development selected on sealed pre-injection forecast loss within the declared supervised regime
Development observation: Phase 2 found 1e-12 channels numerically dominated the objective; selected lambda remained sealed
Known limitation: Objective can be dominated by pathological target scaling; the development regime/split/timing and scenario organization have declared supervision/exposure
Allowed claim: Lambda selection did not use incident outcome labels, but it occurred within a study-specific supervised development regime
Prohibited claim: Lambda selection was wholly label-free, lambda 10 is optimal, or it was selected from final outcomes
Defense answer: We selected among three logarithmically spaced values using pre-injection numeric error shared across arms, without incident outcome labels, inside the declared supervised development regime; Phase 2 limits how strongly that loss can be interpreted.

Exact choice: Target fit requires >=18 of 23 usable lag1 rows
Scientific purpose: Avoid fitting a per-target model on severely incomplete history
Why this exact value/range: About 78% usable rows approximates the study's 80% completeness rule after one lag row
Development observation: Eligibility was sealed and audited
Known limitation: Exact 18/23 cutoff has no external optimum
Allowed claim: It is a model-estimability guard, not an anomaly threshold
Prohibited claim: 18 rows guarantee reliable coefficients
Defense answer: We require roughly eighty percent of the available lagged fit rows so ridge is not fit to a fragment; the exact cutoff is study-specific.

Exact choice: Calibration requires >=9 of 12 normal rows
Scientific purpose: Prevent a threshold quantile from being based on a tiny normal tail
Why this exact value/range: Nine rows is 75% of the held-out block, retaining some tolerance for missingness
Development observation: Calibration eligibility was sealed and audited
Known limitation: Nine observations are still few for Q95-Q99 and exact cutoff is not externally justified
Allowed claim: It is a minimum support condition with uncertainty
Prohibited claim: Nine rows make tail quantiles precise
Defense answer: We require most of the held-out minute to be present; it is a minimum viability guard, and high-quantile uncertainty remains a limitation.

Exact choice: For calibration errors e: mu_e=median(e), s_e=max(IQR(e), epsilon_e), epsilon_e=0.01 primary; r=max(0,(e-mu_e)/s_e)
Source / lineage: GDN error-normalization and BARO robust-scaling principles; the absolute residual floor and one-sided excess score are TD adaptations
Scientific purpose: Make forecast errors comparable across targets and score only excess above the held-out residual center
Why this exact value/range: Median/IQR provide robust center/scale; epsilon_e is an absolute downstream residual floor, separate from the input relative floor and input 1e-12 fallback
Development observation: Residual-floor variants rescaled extreme L thresholds but did not change L-MTL F1; Phase 2 separated them from input scaling
Known limitation: Only 9-12 correlated calibration errors make scale noisy; exact 0.01 is not externally optimal
Allowed claim: Robust residual normalization is principled; the absolute residual floor is study-specific and downstream of input normalization
Prohibited claim: Residual floor changes the input 1e-12 branch or prior work validates epsilon_e=0.01
Defense answer: We center held-out forecast errors by their median and divide by the larger of their IQR or an absolute 0.01 residual floor; this is downstream from the input scaler and has separate sensitivities.

Exact choice: System score = maximum eligible target residual
Source / lineage: TD-v1.3; GDN official evaluator also uses max aggregation, supporting the principle only
Scientific purpose: Detect when any modeled service-channel is strongly anomalous
Why this exact value/range: Max matches an any-component incident alarm and is easy to audit
Alternatives considered: Mean/quantile pooling not registered for primary
Development observation: 1e-12 channels did not alone explain L collapse; extreme channels can dominate individual bins
Known limitation: Sensitive to a single pathological channel and number of targets
Allowed claim: It is an OR-style system alarm under fixed eligibility
Prohibited claim: Max is robust or identifies the root cause
Defense answer: We use max because one severe component should be enough to signal a system incident; that makes single-channel scaling a known limitation.

Exact choice: q in {0.95,0.975,0.99}; selected 0.95 on held-out normal calibration and development macro regime F1
Scientific purpose: Control false-alarm stringency while keeping all selection pre-final and within registered candidates
Why this exact value/range: Three upper-tail levels cover moderate to strict alarms without continuous threshold search
Sensitivity evidence: All q candidates evaluated on development only
Development observation: 0.95 selected for G/L/ALL
Known limitation: Small calibration blocks make tail quantiles discrete; development selection can overfit
Allowed claim: q=.95 is a registered development choice awaiting final confirmation
Prohibited claim: q=.95 is a calibrated universal false-positive rate
Defense answer: We chose among three preregistered tail quantiles on development; with short calibration blocks they are operating points, not exact probability guarantees.

Exact choice: At least 100 pooled normal endpoints for q selection
Scientific purpose: Prevent selecting an extreme quantile from trivial pooled support
Why this exact value/range: 100 gives a round minimum with nominal resolution near one percent
Development observation: Development selection met the gate
Known limitation: Pooling dependent endpoints does not create 100 independent samples; exact count is operational
Allowed claim: It is a minimum support condition, not an IID guarantee
Prohibited claim: 100 endpoints validate tail calibration statistically
Defense answer: We require at least one hundred normal score endpoints before comparing tail thresholds; they are still dependent, so the gate ensures support, not formal precision.

Exact choice: At least 80% of training cases contribute any normal score to q selection
Scientific purpose: Stop a few well-instrumented cases from defining the shared threshold
Why this exact value/range: 80% matches the study's broad completeness convention
Development observation: Development selection met the gate
Known limitation: Case contribution is binary and does not equal balanced endpoint weight
Allowed claim: It guards coverage across cases
Prohibited claim: 80% proves representativeness of all fault/root strata
Defense answer: We require normal scores from at least eighty percent of training cases so threshold selection is not driven by a small convenient subset.

Exact choice: Three consecutive exceedances (streak3)
Scientific purpose: Suppress isolated score spikes before declaring an alarm event
Why this exact value/range: Three bins is a short persistence rule: 15 s under primary binning
Development observation: Trigger and censoring counts changed materially, especially for L-MTL
Known limitation: Event policy affects alert counts but not bin-level detector F1
Allowed claim: It is a registered persistence convention with explicit sensitivity
Prohibited claim: Three is optimal or improves the primary efficacy claim
Defense answer: We require three consecutive exceedances to avoid one-bin alarms; one and five are reported as event-policy sensitivities, not used to retune F1.

Exact choice: Refractory period 300 s
Scientific purpose: Avoid counting one incident repeatedly as many alerts
Why this exact value/range: Five minutes matches the incident-scale observation window and is operationally interpretable
Development observation: Event counts varied strongly with refractory duration
Known limitation: Does not change bin-level detection quality and is not an SLA
Allowed claim: It is an alert-counting convention
Prohibited claim: 300 s is a statistically optimal cooldown
Defense answer: We use five minutes to deduplicate repeated alarms from one episode and disclose 60/600-second counts; it is an operational rule, not detector tuning.

Exact choice: For each channel c, TV_c=mean over valid undirected edges of (z_u,c-z_v,c)^2; system S=max_c TV_c; no comparable edge means UNAVAILABLE
Source / lineage: Graph total-variation/Laplacian principle from Gopalakrishnan, Li and Balakrishnan (CDC 2019); PRIOR SUPPORTS PRINCIPLE, NOT TD'S BINARY GRAPH, MEAN NORMALIZATION OR THRESHOLD
Scientific purpose: Measure disagreement of neighboring node signals as a complementary graph statistic
Why this exact value/range: Squared edge differences are the canonical variation primitive; TD uses a mean over comparable binary edges and a channel maximum for auditable scale control
Sensitivity evidence: Reported separately; no promotion based on outcome
Development observation: Development secondary output does not replace primary C5
Known limitation: Prior theory assumptions and graph weights differ; high TV is not causal localization and isolates/no-edge cases are unavailable
Allowed claim: It is a secondary structural-signal diagnostic using the exact registered mean-edge operator
Prohibited claim: The implemented TD operator is literally unnormalized x^T L x or Graph-TV theory validates the complete C5 detector
Defense answer: Graph TV measures mean squared disagreement across valid observed edges and takes the largest channel; we keep it secondary because our binary graph and noise assumptions do not inherit the paper's guarantees.

Exact choice: MRR is primary C1 localization metric
Source / lineage: Standard information-retrieval ranking metric; TD-v1.3 predeclared endpoint
Scientific purpose: Reward placing the true root high while using the full ranking
Why this exact value/range: One reciprocal rank per case is interpretable and sensitive near the top
Known limitation: MRR averages heterogeneous cases and does not express calibration or causal certainty
Allowed claim: MRR measures ranking quality for the known injected root
Prohibited claim: High MRR proves causal explanation quality
Defense answer: MRR directly scores how high the known injected root appears, with strong emphasis on top positions; secondary metrics show complementary views.

Exact choice: Tie-aware expected reciprocal rank over the root's tie interval
Source / lineage: Explicit TD-v1.3 tie handling; expectation under uniform ordering within an exact tie
Scientific purpose: Avoid arbitrary service-name ordering changing MRR
Why this exact value/range: Expected RR is neutral within an unresolved tie
Alternatives considered: Optimistic or pessimistic tie breaking rejected
Development observation: Development aggregate matched sealed results under the fixed rule
Known limitation: Ties still indicate lack of discrimination
Allowed claim: It makes tied rankings deterministic and fair
Prohibited claim: It resolves the underlying diagnostic ambiguity
Defense answer: When scores tie, we average reciprocal rank across the positions the root could occupy instead of letting a name-order decide the result.

Exact choice: Hit@k and NDCG are secondary
Scientific purpose: Show operational shortlist success and graded rank quality without displacing the prespecified primary
Why this exact value/range: They complement rather than multiply primary claims
Sensitivity evidence: Reported under the registered metric suite
Development observation: Development results were interpreted with MRR primary
Known limitation: Small sample and multiple descriptive endpoints limit standalone interpretation
Allowed claim: They contextualize MRR
Prohibited claim: A favorable secondary metric overrides an unfavorable primary
Defense answer: Hit@k answers whether the root reaches a shortlist and NDCG adds rank context; neither is used to rescue the primary endpoint.

Exact choice: Root absent or method failure contributes score 0
Scientific purpose: Prevent silent removal of hard/data-failure cases from efficacy
Why this exact value/range: Zero is the minimum reciprocal-rank contribution and keeps denominators fixed
Development observation: Development30 denominators remained auditable
Known limitation: Conflates coverage failure with ranking failure, intentionally for end-to-end efficacy
Allowed claim: Reported efficacy includes registered pipeline failures
Prohibited claim: Zero means the method explicitly ranked the root last
Defense answer: If the system cannot rank the known root, we score the case as failure rather than improve results by dropping it.

Exact choice: Development folds grouped by 10 root x fault cells; five folds of two cells; repeats stay together
Source / lineage: TD-v1.3 grouped selection design; block-CV principle supported by Roberts et al. DOI:10.1111/ecog.02881; PRIOR SUPPORTS PRINCIPLE, NOT EXACT FOLDS
Scientific purpose: Reduce leakage and selection optimism from replicated cells
Why this exact value/range: Holding out whole cells is the strongest grouping available within development30 while retaining five selection folds
Sensitivity evidence: Leave-cell winner counts and subgroup checks
Development observation: C1 winner varied across folds/cells, exposing instability
Known limitation: Only 10 cells and same services/fault families remain; not external validation
Allowed claim: Grouping reduces within-cell leakage
Prohibited claim: Five folds are IID or eliminate all selection bias
Defense answer: We hold out complete root-by-fault cells so repeats never split across train and validation; it reduces leakage but does not make thirty cases independent.

Exact choice: Development30 for selection; current-method final60 predictions/labels sealed for prospective frozen-contrast evaluation
Source / lineage: MASTER program, TD-v1.3 staged evidence policy and historical exposure ledger
Scientific purpose: Separate bounded method choice from a one-time frozen evaluation while disclosing prior benchmark exposure
Why this exact value/range: A larger sealed final partition limits additional outcome reuse after freeze, but E1 had already seen TT90 baseline outcomes and post-hoc fusion/strata
Alternatives considered: No random resplitting or final-outcome tuning; never describe the benchmark as clean or untouched
Selection policy: Fixed and sealed for the current method
Sensitivity evidence: Historical exposure ledger plus current-method seal status; no final-outcome sensitivity
Development observation: Historical TT90 outcome exposure is declared; current-method final60 predictions/labels remain unopened
Known limitation: Historical outcome exposure and reuse of the same benchmark limit independence; 60 cases are not a universal power guarantee
Allowed claim: This is a prospectively frozen new contrast on a previously studied benchmark, not clean independent confirmation
Prohibited claim: Final60 is untouched, clean confirmatory evidence, or guarantees significance/generalization
Defense answer: Development selected within the registry; after human freeze, final60 may evaluate the frozen contrasts once, but the defense must disclose that the benchmark was previously studied and is not an untouched test set.

Exact choice: 50,000 paired scenario-block bootstrap replicates over 20 cells
Source / lineage: Block bootstrap principle; Owen arXiv:0712.1111 and dependent-data literature support respecting grouped dependence; PRIOR SUPPORTS PRINCIPLE, NOT EXACT DESIGN
Scientific purpose: Estimate paired uncertainty while resampling the scenario unit rather than individual cases
Why this exact value/range: 50k makes Monte Carlo error negligible relative to sample uncertainty; 20 cells preserve paired structure
Development observation: Not yet applied to final60 in this review
Known limitation: Only 20 blocks; crossed dependencies and finite benchmark scope limit population inference
Allowed claim: Intervals describe the registered scenario population with block-aware uncertainty
Prohibited claim: Bootstrap creates new independent scenarios or proves population generalization
Defense answer: We resample paired scenario cells, not individual rows, and use many replicates to stabilize computation; the dominant uncertainty is the small set of cells.

Exact choice: Two primary contrasts with 97.5% intervals each (Bonferroni family-wise nominal 95%)
Scientific purpose: Keep the two confirmatory graph contrasts in one declared family
Why this exact value/range: Alpha .05 split across two contrasts gives .025 per two-sided interval family
Development observation: No final inference opened
Known limitation: Conservative and does not solve benchmark dependence
Allowed claim: Controls nominal family-wise coverage for the declared contrasts under the procedure
Prohibited claim: It guarantees substantive significance or external validity
Defense answer: We declared two primary contrasts and use Bonferroni-adjusted intervals so the family, not each isolated result, has nominal 95% coverage.

Exact choice: Smallest effect of interest delta = 0.05 MRR
Source / lineage: TD-v1.3; SESOI principle supported by Lakens PMID:28736600; exact 0.05 is study-specific
Scientific purpose: Distinguish practical equivalence/inferiority/superiority from merely nonzero differences
Why this exact value/range: Five MRR points was fixed as a practically meaningful study-scale change, illustrated as six of 60 rank-2 to rank-1 improvements
Development observation: Development differences can be interpreted against but cannot redefine delta
Known limitation: Not tied to an operational SLA and exact value is judgmental
Allowed claim: 0.05 is the prespecified practical threshold for this study
Prohibited claim: 0.05 is universally meaningful or clinically/operationally validated
Defense answer: We fixed five MRR points before final as the smallest study-relevant change; it is a transparent judgment, not a universal SLA.

Exact choice: Signal starvation when >=80% of planned final incidents have empty V or identical round(local/max(local),12) values; all-zero is handled separately as all-tie
Scientific purpose: Make relation attribution inconclusive when the common local signal is absent or non-discriminating in most incidents
Why this exact value/range: The 80% cutoff is a pre-outcome study convention marking widespread rather than occasional starvation
Alternatives considered: Retain all cases and operational scores; do not exclude starved cases or redefine the gate as generic eligibility
Sensitivity evidence: No direct cutoff sensitivity; preflight and development report signal diagnostics
Development observation: Development passed with limitations and did not trigger an all-zero/all-tie primary condition
Known limitation: Exact cutoff has no external optimum and passing does not prove local evidence is strong in every stratum
Allowed claim: The gate conditions strong relation attribution when most planned incidents contain no discriminating local signal
Prohibited claim: It means fewer than 80% of cases are eligible, proves no missing-data bias, or authorizes case removal
Defense answer: If at least eighty percent of planned final incidents have no candidate set or the same normalized local value across candidates, topology attribution is inconclusive; this is a fixed claim guard, not a performance threshold.

Exact choice: Shared preprocessing failure >10% triggers inconclusive/shared-failure handling
Scientific purpose: Prevent a shared loader or feature failure from being mistaken for arm performance
Why this exact value/range: Ten percent is a conservative operational ceiling for pipeline-wide loss
Alternatives considered: Continue normal inference at <=10%; stop/limit claims above
Development observation: Development completed PASS WITH LIMITATIONS rather than tripping this gate
Known limitation: Exact 10% is not externally calibrated and shared failures can cluster
Allowed claim: It is a study governance guard
Prohibited claim: Below 10% means failures are ignorable
Defense answer: We cap shared preprocessing loss at ten percent so a common data failure cannot masquerade as an algorithm result; the threshold is operational, not inferential.

Exact choice: C5 lambda-selection eligibility requires >=80% development cases with valid objective contribution
Scientific purpose: Prevent a shared hyperparameter from being selected on a narrow subset
Why this exact value/range: Matches broader 80% case-coverage convention
Development observation: Primary selection completed; Phase 2 showed contribution imbalance despite case eligibility
Known limitation: Binary case eligibility does not prevent a few channels dominating numeric loss
Allowed claim: It ensures broad case participation, not balanced influence
Prohibited claim: 80% eligibility proves the objective is well behaved
Defense answer: We require contributions from at least eighty percent of development cases before selecting lambda; Phase 2 shows this does not by itself prevent scale dominance.

Exact choice: Predictions and selections sealed before final labels; no silent outcome-driven mutation; any material pre-freeze change returns to D for versioning, review and exposure logging
Source / lineage: MASTER program, TD-v1.3 and CURRENT-STATE evidence gates
Scientific purpose: Limit researcher degrees of freedom while preserving the distinction between development exposure and opening final outcomes
Why this exact value/range: Freezing after bounded diagnostics prevents silent redesign; TD still permits a reviewed finite-registry amendment before final freeze with an extra-attempt/exposure record
Alternatives considered: Reviewed pre-freeze amendment versus post-final exploratory versioning
Sensitivity evidence: Hashes, seals and read-only Phase 1/2 analyses
Development observation: No current finding mandates TD-v1.4 and final60 remains unopened
Known limitation: A reviewed amendment would increase development selection exposure and require re-review, but would not by itself open final60
Allowed claim: The current method and limitations remain sealed unless Minh authorizes the TD return/amendment path
Prohibited claim: No amendment is ever permitted, or any development amendment automatically consumes/opens final60
Defense answer: We do not silently retune after seeing development outcomes. A material pre-freeze change is possible only through a versioned return to Task D, review and explicit exposure logging; that raises selection exposure but does not itself open final60.
